doc.title: George Russell — Smithsonian Jazz Oral History

chapter: Later years: recordings, Alice and the book
title: The African Game and the Grammy
summary: Russell describes the Boston-assembled band behind The African Game, held back by Bruce Lundvall, which he thinks deserved a Grammy.

story.theme_name: In the studio: making records, then and now
story.community_name: Record labels, producers and the business of making albums

blocks.x: The ’80s seemed to be a pretty good time for music and for you, musically. You had a number of recordings that came out in the ’80s. Did you do many live performances during the decade of the ’80s as well?
If I did, they were all in Europe. I must have.
There was one that I recall here in the Boston area, at Emmanuel Church was it? The So What – that’s where the So What recording was made.

That was a band that was put together with a number of people from New England Conservatory, but also others out in the street, the streets of Boston. It was called African Game. I like to think that that’s one of my best, because of its visits to different places and different feelings. It turned out very well. Bruce Lundvall has kept it a secret for many, many years. That secret’s going to explode soon.
That’s Bruce Lundvall of Blue Note Records?

It was a – I remember that it was a commission for about 25 musicians? There were two Grammy nominations that came forward, once the record actually came out itself. I think one was for best big band performance, and one was for best instrumental arrangement. It was a very fine record. The vertical form was prevalent, strong, throughout, the rhythmic aspect of it, as well as all of the orchestrations, a fantastic record.

I don’t believe much in giveaways in terms of – that happen when people perform and it’s an audience of all kinds of people that are hired as raiders. I think African Game deserved a Grammy, not just two recognitions. It deserved a Grammy, because what got the Grammy was not anywhere near what African Game is. I’m glad I’m giving you the high down and the lowdown. Okay?
